title: Mac Running Slow? 5 Fixes Before You Buy a New One
excerpt: Spinning beach balls and slow boots on macOS — storage, login items, and the one upgrade that matters most.

steps.heading: 1. Free up disk space (macOS needs 15% free)
steps.body: Apple menu → About This Mac → More Info → Storage Settings. Clear caches, old iOS backups, and Downloads. A nearly-full drive slows everything because macOS has no room for swap and updates.

steps.heading: 2. Trim login items and background apps
steps.body: System Settings → General → Login Items. Remove updaters, chat apps, and anything you don't use daily. Then check Activity Monitor for runaway processes eating CPU — browsers with 40 tabs are the usual suspect.

steps.heading: 3. Update macOS and reset the SMC/NVRAM if behavior is weird
steps.body: Install all pending updates first. For Intel Macs with fan, battery, or sleep weirdness, reset the SMC and NVRAM (Apple's support pages have the exact key combos per model). Apple Silicon Macs just need a restart.

whenToCall: Keyboard, trackpad, battery swelling, or screen issues — hardware needs hands on it.
You need data recovered from a Mac that won't boot.
It's a work Mac needing 365, VPN, and device management configured.

faqs.q: Should I use a Mac cleaner app?
faqs.a: No — most are junk or adware. macOS Storage Settings plus Activity Monitor do the job free.

faqs.q: Is my old Intel Mac still worth fixing?
faqs.a: For browsing and Office, often yes with an SSD and fresh macOS. For video work or anything Apple Silicon–only, do the replacement math honestly — we'll tell you straight.

title: Laptop Overheating or Shutting Off? Cool It Down Safely
excerpt: Hot base, loud fans, random shutdowns — vents, thermal paste decisions, and when heat means hardware failure.

steps.heading: 1. Give it air and clean the vents
steps.body: Use it on a hard flat surface — beds and couches smother intakes. With the machine off, blast vents with short bursts of compressed air. A surprising amount of 'dying' laptops are just carpet-lint insulation.

steps.heading: 2. Check what's cooking the CPU
steps.body: Task Manager (or Activity Monitor) sorted by CPU will show the culprit: stuck updaters, runaway browser tabs, or a scan loop. End the offender and watch temperatures drop within minutes.

steps.heading: 3. Adjust power and update drivers
steps.body: Switch to Balanced power mode, install BIOS/firmware and chipset updates from the manufacturer, and confirm fans actually spin. A dead fan plus heavy use equals shutdowns — that's protection circuitry saving your data.

whenToCall: It shuts off within minutes even at idle — likely fan failure or dried thermal paste.
You smell burning or see swelling (battery) — stop using it and call immediately.
It's a work machine and downtime costs money — same-day remote diagnosis from $75.

faqs.q: Do cooling pads actually help?
faqs.a: A little — 3 to 5 degrees, plus they enforce good airflow habits. They can't fix a dead fan or caked heatsink, though.

faqs.q: Is repasting the CPU worth it?
faqs.a: On machines 4+ years old, fresh thermal paste can drop temps 10–15°C. It's a $125/hr bench job, usually under an hour plus parts.

title: Second Monitor Not Detected? Fix It in 5 Minutes
excerpt: No signal, wrong resolution, or Windows ignoring your monitor — cable order, input source, and driver fixes.

steps.heading: 1. Check input source and cable seating first
steps.body: Cycle the monitor's input button to the port you're actually using (HDMI 1 vs 2 trips up everyone). Reseat both ends of the cable, and try a different cable — cheap adapters fail silently and often.

steps.heading: 2. Force detection in display settings
steps.body: Windows: Settings → System → Display → Multiple displays → Detect. Set to Extend (not Duplicate) for real two-screen work. On Mac: System Settings → Displays → hold Option to reveal Detect Displays.

steps.heading: 3. Update graphics drivers, not Windows
steps.body: Get the driver from Intel/NVIDIA/AMD directly — Windows Update ships months-old graphics drivers. A fresh driver fixes most 'worked yesterday' detection failures after updates.

whenToCall: The port itself is dead across cables and monitors — likely board-level repair.
You need a full office setup: dual monitors, dock, webcam, and cable management.
It's a Mac with dongle chaos — we'll spec the one-dock setup that just works.

faqs.q: HDMI or DisplayPort — does it matter?
faqs.a: For 1080p either is fine. For 4K at 60Hz+, use DisplayPort or HDMI 2.0+ cables — old HDMI cables silently cap you at 30Hz, which feels laggy.

faqs.q: Why is everything huge/blurry on the second monitor?
faqs.a: Mismatched scaling. Set each display's scale individually in Display settings (100% on the external is usually right) and sign out and back in once.

title: Camera or Mic Dead on Zoom/Teams? The 4-Minute Fix
excerpt: They can't see you, they can't hear you — privacy shutters, app permissions, and the default-device trap.
symptoms: Works in one app but not another

steps.heading: 1. Check the physical shutter and mute switches
steps.body: Slide the webcam cover open and check headset mic-mute switches — half of all 'broken camera' tickets end here. Laptops with kill switches (Framework, some Lenovos) need the function-key toggle too.

steps.heading: 2. Fix app permissions
steps.body: Windows: Settings → Privacy → Camera/Microphone → allow desktop apps. Mac: System Settings → Privacy → Camera/Microphone → check your meeting app. Browsers need per-site permission too — click the camera icon in the address bar.

steps.heading: 3. Set the right default devices
steps.body: In Zoom/Teams settings, explicitly pick your mic, speaker, and camera instead of 'Same as System'. USB headsets that get unplugged once silently reroute everything to laptop speakers — this setting prevents the loop.

whenToCall: Camera vanished from Device Manager entirely — likely hardware or driver failure.
You need a whole meeting-room setup: camera, mics, speakers that work for everyone.
It's a work machine locked down by policies blocking device access.

faqs.q: Why does it work in Zoom but not Teams?
faqs.a: Per-app permissions. Granting the camera to Zoom doesn't grant it to Teams or Chrome — each app needs its own permission in system settings.

faqs.q: Should I buy an external webcam?
faqs.a: If you meet daily, yes — a $60 external cam beats every built-in laptop camera. We can recommend one that matches your lighting and room.

title: Bluetooth Won't Connect on Windows? Pair It Properly
excerpt: Headphones, mice, and keyboards that refuse to pair — the remove-re-pair cycle plus the two services that must run.
symptoms: Device won't appear in pairing list

steps.heading: 1. Remove, restart, re-pair cleanly
steps.body: Settings → Bluetooth → remove the device. Turn the accessory fully off, restart the PC, then put the accessory in pairing mode (usually hold power 5+ seconds until it flashes) and pair fresh. Layered pairings from old attempts conflict constantly.

steps.heading: 2. Check the Bluetooth services
steps.body: Win+R → services.msc → confirm Bluetooth Audio Gateway, Bluetooth Support Service, and Bluetooth User Support Service are Running and Automatic. Updates flip these to Manual more often than you'd think.

steps.heading: 3. Update or reinstall the Bluetooth driver
steps.body: Device Manager → Bluetooth → right-click adapter → Update driver. If that fails, Uninstall device (keep driver files unchecked), reboot, and let Windows rediscover it cleanly.

whenToCall: No Bluetooth adapter appears in Device Manager at all — possible hardware failure.
You need office-wide headsets, conference mics, or multi-device setups standardized.
It's a work machine where peripherals must meet security policy.

faqs.q: Why does my headset pair with my phone but not my PC?
faqs.a: Many headsets remember one active connection. Disconnect from the phone first (or turn phone Bluetooth off temporarily), then pair to the PC.

faqs.q: Is a USB Bluetooth dongle a real fix?
faqs.a: Yes — a $15 dongle bypasses flaky built-in adapters entirely. Match Bluetooth 5.x for the best range and audio quality.

title: Gmail Says Storage Full? Reclaim Gigabytes in 15 Minutes
excerpt: 15GB shared across Gmail, Drive, and Photos — find the space hogs and stop paying for junk.
symptoms: Can't send email — storage full error

steps.heading: 1. See what's actually eating the space
steps.body: Go to one.google.com/storage. It's almost always Photos and old Drive files with big videos — email itself is rarely the culprit. Knowing the split saves you from deleting the wrong things.

steps.heading: 2. Purge the big, obvious junk
steps.body: In Gmail search: has:attachment larger:10M — delete ancient newsletters with attachments, then empty Trash and Spam (they still count!). In Drive, sort by storage used and nuke old installers and duplicate videos.

steps.heading: 3. Fix Photos before paying for storage
steps.body: In Google Photos, use Manage Storage → review large videos and blurry shots. Switch future backups to Storage Saver quality. Most people reclaim 5–10GB here alone — often enough to cancel the upgrade.

whenToCall: It's a business account where mail flow stopping means money stopping.
You need a real archival strategy — local backup plus retention rules — not just deletions.
Migration to Microsoft 365 with proper mailbox sizing is overdue anyway.

faqs.q: Does emptying Trash actually free space?
faqs.a: Yes — Gmail Trash and Spam count against your quota for 30 days until auto-deleted. Empty them manually for instant space.

faqs.q: Should I just pay for Google One?
faqs.a: If you've cleaned up and genuinely need it, $2/mo for 100GB is fair. But most 'full storage' cases are 80% junk — clean first, pay second.

title: Outlook Keeps Asking for Your Password? Break the Loop
excerpt: Daily password prompts that never stick — credential cache, MFA app vs SMS, and the profile rebuild that ends it.

steps.heading: 1. Clear stale credentials
steps.body: Control Panel → Credential Manager → Windows Credentials → remove every Outlook/Office/Microsoft entry. A changed password plus a cached old token is the classic loop — Outlook keeps offering the dead token.

steps.heading: 2. Switch MFA to the Authenticator app
steps.body: SMS-code MFA plus Outlook's modern auth argue constantly. Approve sign-ins from Microsoft Authenticator instead — then sign into Outlook fresh once. The loop usually ends here.

steps.heading: 3. Rebuild the Outlook profile if it persists
steps.body: Control Panel → Mail → Show Profiles → Add a new profile, set it default. A corrupt profile keeps requesting auth no matter what you type. Your mail re-downloads from the server — nothing is lost.

whenToCall: The whole office loops at once — likely Conditional Access, expired cert, or license issue.
It's tied to a migration or tenant change needing admin-side fixes.
You want MFA rolled out properly so the loop never comes back.

faqs.q: Why did this start right after I changed my password?
faqs.a: Every cached copy of the old password — Outlook, phone mail apps, Teams — fights the new one. Update all devices the same day and clear Credential Manager.

faqs.q: Is 'remember my credentials' safe to check?
faqs.a: On your own encrypted device, yes. On shared or public machines, never — use webmail instead.

title: Video Calls Keep Freezing? Fix Your Connection for Meetings
excerpt: Robotic audio and frozen faces on Zoom/Teams — bandwidth vs Wi-Fi vs CPU, and the settings that stabilize calls.
symptoms: Fine for browsing, bad for meetings

steps.heading: 1. Figure out which leg is broken
steps.body: Run a speed test during a bad call: under 5 Mbps up means bandwidth; good speeds but bad calls means Wi-Fi or CPU. Plug into Ethernet for one call as the control test — if Ethernet is perfect, it's your Wi-Fi, full stop.

steps.heading: 2. Move to 5GHz and kill the competition
steps.body: Join the 5GHz band near the router, pause cloud backups and 4K streams during calls, and close the 40-tab browser. Meetings need steady upload — one Dropbox sync can strangle them.

steps.heading: 3. Lower the load: 720p, backgrounds off, wired headset
steps.body: Drop to 720p, turn off virtual backgrounds (they eat CPU), and use a wired or dedicated headset. Each change removes one failure point — together they fix most 'bad meeting' setups.

whenToCall: Ethernet is also bad — likely ISP line issues needing documented speed tests and a provider fight.
Your office needs pro treatment: dedicated AP, QoS rules, or Ethernet runs.
It's Teams-specific across the company — tenant or policy issue, not your Wi-Fi.

faqs.q: How much speed do video calls actually need?
faqs.a: About 3–5 Mbps up/down per 720p call. The killer is stability, not speed — jitter and packet loss freeze calls on 200 Mbps connections too.

faqs.q: Wired headset or Bluetooth?
faqs.a: Wired for important calls — Bluetooth adds latency and another dropout source. Save Bluetooth for listening, not presenting.

title: Smart TV Won't Connect to Wi-Fi? Stream Again Tonight
excerpt: Endless buffering wheels and 'network error' on Netflix — TV Wi-Fi quirks, DNS fixes, and when to just wire it.
symptoms: TV can't find the Wi-Fi network

steps.heading: 1. Cold-boot the TV (not standby)
steps.body: Unplug the TV for 60 seconds — the remote's power button only sleeps it. Stale network stacks survive sleep for weeks; a real power cycle clears most 'suddenly stopped working' cases.

steps.heading: 2. Forget the network and rejoin 2.4GHz first
steps.body: In TV network settings, forget your Wi-Fi and reconnect — try 2.4GHz for reliability through walls. TVs have weak antennas; the band your phone loves is often the one your TV can't hold.

steps.heading: 3. Wire it or set manual DNS
steps.body: Best fix: Ethernet or a powerline adapter to the TV — streaming boxes stop competing for airtime entirely. Quick alternative: set DNS manually to 8.8.8.8, which fixes ISP-DNS quirks that stall app logins.

whenToCall: Every device buffers, not just the TV — whole-network problem needing diagnosis.
You want clean TV-wall Ethernet runs or an access point near the living room.
Streaming logins fail across apps — possible account, DNS, or ISP issue.

faqs.q: Should I use a Fire Stick instead of the TV apps?
faqs.a: Usually yes — sticks get updates years longer than built-in TV apps, and their Wi-Fi chips are better. A $40 stick often outperforms a $1,000 TV's smart platform.

faqs.q: Why does Netflix fail but YouTube work?
faqs.a: Different servers and DNS paths. Try the manual DNS step, sign out/in of the app, and check for a TV firmware update.

title: Facebook Account Hacked? Recover It Before They Lock You Out
excerpt: Unknown logins, changed email, friends getting scam messages 'from you' — the recovery race, in order.
symptoms: Can't log in with your password
Friends report scam messages from you

steps.heading: 1. Start recovery from a device you've used before
steps.body: Go to facebook.com/hacked on your own phone or computer — recovery succeeds far more often from recognized devices and networks. Follow the identity steps immediately; every hour gives the attacker time to change recovery options.

steps.heading: 2. Kick every session and check the email chain
steps.body: Once back in: Settings → Security → Where you're logged in → Log out of all sessions. Then verify your email and phone number are still yours — attackers swap these first so password resets go to them.

steps.heading: 3. Warn your contacts and lock the blast radius
steps.body: Post that you were hacked and to ignore money requests. Then secure the email account behind Facebook (it's the master key), turn on two-factor with an authenticator app, and review connected apps for anything you don't recognize.

whenToCall: Recovery options were all changed and automated recovery fails — we escalate with documentation.
Money already moved (gift cards, Zelle, crypto) — time matters, plus a police report for the paper trail.
It's a business page with ad spend attached — hijacked pages burn money hourly.

faqs.q: My friends sent money to the scammer. Can it be recovered?
faqs.a: Sometimes via the bank or card issuer if reported within days — gift cards and crypto are usually gone. File a police report regardless; platforms and banks ask for it.

faqs.q: How do I stop this happening again?
faqs.a: Authenticator-app two-factor, unique password via a manager, and login alerts on. SMS two-factor alone gets SIM-swapped — the app version doesn't.

title: "Your Package Couldn't Be Delivered" Text? It's a Smishing Scam
excerpt: Fake USPS, UPS, and toll-road texts spiked across Tampa — how to spot them in 5 seconds and what to do if you clicked.
symptoms: Text about a package you didn't order
Link to pay a small redelivery fee

steps.heading: 1. Apply the 5-second test
steps.body: Real carriers don't text links demanding payment to release packages, and toll agencies don't collect by text. Unknown sender + urgency + link + payment = scam, every time. Delete it.

steps.heading: 2. Never click — verify separately
steps.body: Expecting something? Open the carrier's app or type the address yourself — never the texted link. Scam sites mimic tracking pages pixel-perfectly to harvest cards and credentials.

steps.heading: 3. Report and block
steps.body: Forward the text to 7726 (SPAM) on any US carrier, then block the sender. On iPhone use Report Junk; on Android use Spam & block. Reports feed carrier filters that protect everyone else.

whenToCall: You entered card or login details — treat it as identity theft: freeze, dispute, reset.
It's hitting company phones and staff keep clicking — you need training plus mobile protection.
Money already moved — bank dispute plus police report, fast.

faqs.q: I clicked but didn't enter anything. Am I safe?
faqs.a: Almost certainly — but close the tab, clear that browser's data, and watch for follow-up texts. No credentials entered means nothing to steal.

faqs.q: Why am I suddenly getting so many?
faqs.a: Your number leaked in a breach or was auto-dialed in bulk. It rarely means you're specifically targeted — block, report, and don't engage, since replies confirm a live number.

title: Is Coffee-Shop Wi-Fi Safe? The 5-Minute Safety Setup
excerpt: Airports, hotels, and cafes across Tampa Bay — what attackers actually do on open Wi-Fi and the three settings that neutralize it.
symptoms: Banking or work on public networks

steps.heading: 1. Use your phone hotspot instead whenever you can
steps.body: Cellular data beats any public Wi-Fi for security with zero setup. For laptop work on the go, hotspotting is the single best habit — save public Wi-Fi for casual browsing only.

steps.heading: 2. Verify the network name and use a VPN for anything sensitive
steps.body: Attackers broadcast 'Free_Coffee_Shop_WiFi' next to the real one — ask staff for the exact name. For email, banking, or work, run a reputable VPN; it encrypts everything even if the network is hostile.

steps.heading: 3. Turn on the firewall and forget the network after
steps.body: Enable your OS firewall (it's often off on Windows Home), disable auto-join for public networks, and Forget the network when you leave. Auto-join makes your laptop shout for that network forever — anywhere.

whenToCall: You entered banking credentials on a network you now suspect — assume compromise and act.
Your team works remotely from anywhere — you need managed VPN, not hope.
A work laptop touched hostile networks and now behaves oddly.

faqs.q: Is hotel Wi-Fi with a password safe?
faqs.a: Safer than open, but everyone in the hotel shares that password — treat it as public. VPN still recommended for sensitive work.

faqs.q: Free VPNs — good enough?
faqs.a: No. Free VPNs monetize by logging and selling exactly the traffic you're hiding. A reputable paid VPN costs less per month than one coffee.

title: Has Your Password Already Leaked? Check in 2 Minutes
excerpt: Billions of credentials circulate from past breaches. Look yours up safely and fix what matters first.
symptoms: Got a 'your info was breached' email

steps.heading: 1. Check your email on Have I Been Pwned
steps.body: Type your address at haveibeenpwned.com — it lists every public breach containing it, without you entering any password. Note which breaches included passwords (not just emails).

steps.heading: 2. Change the important ones first, uniquely
steps.body: Email first (it's the master key), then banking, Microsoft/Apple/Google, and anything reused elsewhere. Generate each fresh in your password manager — never rotate one password to another reused one.

steps.heading: 3. Turn on breach alerts going forward
steps.body: Enable monitoring in your password manager and alerts on key accounts. Future breaches then ping you the week they happen instead of surprising you years later.

whenToCall: A breach included financial data or SSN — you need freezes, not just new passwords.
It's a work email in the breach — assume credential-stuffing attempts against company logins.
You want the whole team audited and moved to a manager properly.

faqs.q: Is Have I Been Pwned safe to use?
faqs.a: Yes — run by security researcher Troy Hunt, it only takes your email (never a password) and is the industry-standard lookup.

faqs.q: My old MySpace password leaked. Should I care?
faqs.a: Only if you reused it anywhere since. Attackers automate exactly that: old password → try it on email, banks, and shops. Unique passwords make old leaks worthless.

title: OneDrive Says Storage Full? Fix It Without Paying (Yet)
excerpt: Stopped syncing, red X icons, 'not enough space' — find the hogs across OneDrive, Outlook, and Teams.

steps.heading: 1. Check which bucket is full
steps.body: OneDrive, Outlook mailbox, and Teams/SharePoint share your 365 quota. Check OneDrive Settings → Account for the split — the fix for a 40GB mailbox differs completely from a 40GB photo dump.

steps.heading: 2. Clear the silent hogs
steps.body: Empty OneDrive Recycle Bin (it holds files for 93 days against your quota), unsubscribe from giant shared folders, and move personal videos out. In Outlook, sort by size and archive ancient attachments.

steps.heading: 3. Use Files On-Demand instead of more storage
steps.body: Right-click OneDrive → Settings → turn on Files On-Demand, then Free up space on big folders. Files stay visible and download on open — quota and disk space both recover without deleting anything.

whenToCall: It's a shared mailbox or SharePoint site hitting limits — needs admin-side retention and archival.
Sync broke during cleanup — red errors, conflicts multiplying.
You genuinely outgrew the plan — we'll right-size licenses instead of overpaying.

faqs.q: Do deleted OneDrive files count against storage?
faqs.a: Yes, until the Recycle Bin is emptied — up to 93 days. Empty it manually for instant space, and check the second-stage bin too.

faqs.q: Should I just buy more storage?
faqs.a: After cleanup, maybe. But most 'full' OneDrives are 50%+ recycle bin and duplicates — buying storage for trash is a subscription to your own junk.

title: "File Is Locked for Editing" in Excel? Unlock It Properly
excerpt: OneDrive/SharePoint Excel locks, ghost sessions, and co-authoring conflicts — get everyone editing again.
symptoms: Locked for editing by another user
Ghost lock from someone who left

steps.heading: 1. Check for the ghost session first
steps.body: Someone closed a laptop with the file open — the lock lingers ~10 minutes. Wait, then have everyone fully close Excel (not minimize) and retry. Most locks evaporate on their own.

steps.heading: 2. Open in Excel for the web to bypass it
steps.body: In SharePoint/OneDrive, open the file in the browser version. Web Excel supports real co-authoring and ignores most desktop locks — edit there, and the desktop copy syncs after.

steps.heading: 3. Clear Upload Center cache and check out status
steps.body: Stuck locks often come from a jammed upload cache or a file left Checked Out. Clear the Office Document Cache and confirm nobody has it checked out in the library.

whenToCall: Locks recur daily on shared workbooks — the file needs restructuring or a real database.
Permissions are tangled — people locked out who should be in, or vice versa.
Version history shows data loss from conflicting saves.

faqs.q: Why does it say I'm locking my own file?
faqs.a: Your own crashed session still holds the lock. Wait 10 minutes or open in Excel for the web, which handles session recovery gracefully.

faqs.q: Should we stop sharing Excel files this way?
faqs.a: If 3+ people edit daily, consider moving the workflow to SharePoint lists, Planner, or a proper database. Shared workbooks are a conflict machine at scale.

title: Paying for Microsoft 365 Licenses You Don't Use? Audit in 20 Minutes
excerpt: Ex-employees, duplicate plans, and premium licenses on break-room PCs — the quarterly cleanup that pays for itself.
symptoms: Nobody knows what each plan includes

steps.heading: 1. Export the license list and flag the dead weight
steps.body: Admin center → Billing → Licenses → export. Cross-reference against current staff: every ex-employee, shared mailbox with a license, and test account is money on fire. Convert leavers to shared mailboxes (free) before deleting.

steps.heading: 2. Downgrade the over-licensed
steps.body: Break-room PCs and single-purpose accounts don't need Business Premium. Match licenses to actual needs: Basic for email-only, Standard for desktop apps, Premium only where security features are genuinely used.

steps.heading: 3. Kill duplicates and set a quarterly reminder
steps.body: Same user with two plans, Teams Exploratory trials that converted to paid, duplicate tenants from an old IT guy — remove them all. Then calendar a 20-minute license review every quarter; drift restarts the day you stop looking.

whenToCall: The tenant is a mess of trials, duplicates, and mystery charges — we untangle and document it.
You need true-up before renewal — an hour of cleanup routinely saves hundreds yearly.
Offboarding is manual chaos — we automate it so licenses die with the exit interview.

faqs.q: How much do unused licenses typically cost?
faqs.a: One forgotten Business Standard is $150+/year. We routinely find 3–8 dead licenses per small tenant — that's a free month of Managed IT sitting in the couch cushions.

faqs.q: Can I just delete ex-employee accounts?
faqs.a: Convert to shared mailbox first to keep the email history, then remove the license. Deleting outright can orphan OneDrive data after 30 days.

title: External Drive Not Showing Up? Recover Access Safely
excerpt: Plugged in, spinning, invisible — USB power, drive letters, and the order that protects your data.

steps.heading: 1. Rule out power and ports
steps.body: Plug directly into the PC (no hubs), try a rear USB port on desktops, and use the original cable — big drives need more power than front-panel ports and long cables deliver. Listen: spinning with clicks is very different from silent.

steps.heading: 2. Look in Disk Management before anything else
steps.body: Right-click Start → Disk Management. If the drive appears without a letter, right-click → Change Drive Letter. If it shows as RAW or Unallocated, stop — that's corruption or partition damage, and every further click risks more.

steps.heading: 3. Never initialize or format a drive with data on it
steps.body: Windows will offer to initialize or format the 'broken' drive. Decline. Those operations destroy the map to your files. If the data matters, image the drive first or hand it to a pro before any write operation.

whenToCall: Clicking, beeping, or grinding — power it off; that's physical failure.
Disk Management shows RAW/Unallocated and the data matters.
It's the only copy of anything important — we'll recover it and build you a real 3-2-1 backup.

faqs.q: It works on my TV but not my PC. Why?
faqs.a: Different filesystem support. TVs read exFAT/FAT32; PCs may balk at Mac-formatted (HFS+/APFS) drives without drivers. The drive is usually fine — it's a format mismatch.

faqs.q: Should I keep using a drive that disappeared once?
faqs.a: Only after a full health check and only for non-critical data. A drive that vanishes once is auditioning to vanish permanently — replace it for anything important.

title: Google Photos Full? Save 10GB Without Losing Memories
excerpt: Blurry duplicates, 4K videos, and screenshots eating your quota — the cleanup order that actually works.
symptoms: Paying for storage full of screenshots

steps.heading: 1. Let Google find the junk first
steps.body: Photos → Storage → Review large photos and videos, blurry photos, and screenshots. Delete in bulk — screenshots and memes are the low-hanging gigabytes for almost everyone.

steps.heading: 2. Switch future backups to Storage Saver
steps.body: Photos Settings → Backup quality → Storage Saver. Slight compression invisible on phones, roughly half the space. Keep Original quality only for the DSLR archive that earns it.

steps.heading: 3. Download the keepers locally, then empty trash
steps.body: Use Google Takeout for a full local copy of what matters, verify it opens, then empty Photos trash (items count against quota for 60 days). Now you have 3-2-1 instead of 1-0-0.

whenToCall: Years of business data or photos with no backup anywhere but Google — we'll build the local + cloud archive.
A loved one's account is locked, full, or scheduled for deletion.
Your business runs on shared photo libraries needing real organization.

faqs.q: Will Storage Saver ruin my photos?
faqs.a: For phone viewing and prints up to 8x10, no visible difference. Pixel-peepers with mirrorless cameras should keep Originals — everyone else saves gigabytes.

faqs.q: What happens when Google deletes inactive accounts?
faqs.a: Accounts inactive 2+ years can be deleted with everything in them. Activity plus a local Takeout copy makes this a non-issue.

title: iPhone Won't Back Up to iCloud? Fix It Tonight
excerpt: 'iPhone Not Backed Up' warnings and failed overnight backups — storage, Wi-Fi, and the settings that unstick it.
symptoms: iPhone hasn't backed up in weeks

steps.heading: 1. Make room: it's almost always storage
steps.body: Settings → your name → iCloud → Manage Storage. The next backup needs free space equal to the backup size. Trim old device backups, large message attachments, and app data you don't need — or step up to iCloud+ 50GB for a dollar.

steps.heading: 2. Plug in, lock, and join Wi-Fi overnight
steps.body: iCloud backup needs power + locked screen + Wi-Fi simultaneously. Plug into a real charger (not a weak car USB), join office Wi-Fi, lock the screen, and leave it. Daytime manual backups fight you; overnight ones just work.

steps.heading: 3. Toggle iCloud Backup off and on if it's stuck
steps.body: Settings → your name → iCloud Backup → toggle off, restart the phone, toggle on, tap Back Up Now. This clears the stuck snapshot state without deleting anything already backed up.

whenToCall: The phone is full, failing, or has 64GB of 'Other' nobody can explain.
You're moving to a new iPhone and the transfer keeps failing.
Critical business files exist only on one aging device — we'll archive them properly.

faqs.q: Is the free 5GB iCloud tier enough?
faqs.a: For almost nobody with photos. iCloud+ 50GB costs $0.99/month — the cheapest insurance you'll ever buy. Check what you're actually paying for first in Settings.

faqs.q: iTunes/Finder backup or iCloud?
faqs.a: Both, ideally: iCloud for nightly automation, a computer backup before trips and iOS updates. Two copies, two places — the 3-2-1 starter pack.

title: Customer Wi-Fi for Your Business? Do It Without Risking the Office
excerpt: Cafes, salons, waiting rooms — guest internet that markets you instead of exposing your point-of-sale and files.
symptoms: Guests on the same network as payments
No idea who uses the network

steps.heading: 1. Never share the office network — isolate guests
steps.body: Create a separate guest SSID with client isolation so visitors can't see each other, your printers, or (critically) your point-of-sale system. One shared password for everything is how card data walks out the door.

steps.heading: 2. Add a captive portal with your branding
steps.body: A simple splash page (logo + terms + optional email signup) looks professional, covers you legally, and builds a marketing list. Most business access points include this free — it's just never turned on.

steps.heading: 3. Throttle guests and schedule hours
steps.body: Cap guest bandwidth so a teenager's downloads can't stall your card reader. Set guest Wi-Fi hours to match business hours — an open network at 3am serves nobody but loiterers.

whenToCall: You take card payments — segmentation isn't optional for PCI peace of mind.
You need coverage across a patio, warehouse, or multi-room space.
You want the email list, analytics, and multi-location management done right.

faqs.q: Can guests hack us through the guest network?
faqs.a: Not with proper isolation — they get internet only, no path to office devices. Without isolation, yes, trivially. The setting is the whole ballgame.

faqs.q: What hardware do we need?
faqs.a: One business-grade access point covers most small spaces ($150–$300 installed). We spec Ubiquiti/TP-Link Omada gear that includes portals and throttling without subscriptions.

title: Chrome Eating All Your RAM? Speed It Up in 10 Minutes
excerpt: 40 tabs, crawling pages, fans screaming — tab discipline, extension audit, and the settings that halve memory use.

steps.heading: 1. Turn on Memory Saver and close the tab hoard
steps.body: Chrome Settings → Performance → turn on Memory Saver so inactive tabs sleep. Then bookmark the keepers (Ctrl+Shift+D saves all open tabs to a folder) and close the rest. Tab hoarding is the #1 browser slowdown — no shame, just fix it.

steps.heading: 2. Audit extensions ruthlessly
steps.body: Go to chrome://extensions and remove everything you don't recognize or haven't used this month. Each extension runs constantly; coupon finders and duplicate ad blockers are notorious hogs. Keep one ad blocker and your password manager.

steps.heading: 3. Clear the cruft and check for software hijack
steps.body: Clear cached images/files (keep passwords and history), then run Chrome's built-in cleanup: Settings → Reset settings → Clean up computer → Find harmful software. Hijacked search engines live here.

whenToCall: Slowness persists across browsers — it's the PC, not Chrome (see our slow-PC guide).
Pop-ups and redirects survive cleanup — likely adware needing real removal.
It's a work machine where extensions must meet policy — we standardize and lock them.

faqs.q: How many tabs is too many?
faqs.a: With Memory Saver on, even 50+ is fine on 16GB RAM. On 8GB or less, keep it under 15 active or expect swapping and fan noise.

faqs.q: Edge vs Chrome — should I switch?
faqs.a: Edge uses the same engine with better memory management on Windows and vertical tabs built in. Your extensions and passwords import in two minutes.

title: Windows Search Shows Nothing? Rebuild It in 5 Minutes
excerpt: Blank results, missing files, indexing stuck — restart the service, rebuild the index, and check the exclusions.

steps.heading: 1. Restart Windows Search service
steps.body: Ctrl+Shift+Esc → Details tab → end SearchHost.exe (Windows 11) or SearchIndexer.exe. It restarts automatically. This clears the stuck state behind most sudden search failures.

steps.heading: 2. Run the Search troubleshooter
steps.body: Settings → System → Troubleshoot → Other troubleshooters → Search and Indexing → Run. Let it detect permission and index problems automatically — it fixes the common ones silently.

steps.heading: 3. Rebuild the index overnight
steps.body: Control Panel → Indexing Options → Advanced → Rebuild. It takes hours on big drives, so start it at bedtime. Check that your User folder is in Included Locations first — excluded folders never appear in results.

whenToCall: Search broke across an office after an update — likely policy or profile corruption.
Outlook search specifically is broken — different index, different fix.
You need Everything/ESE-style instant search deployed across workstations.

faqs.q: Why is indexing stuck at 0%?
faqs.a: Usually a corrupt catalog or a dying drive slowing reads to a crawl. Rebuild once; if it sticks again, check drive health before anything else.

faqs.q: Should I just use the Everything app?
faqs.a: For filename search it's instant and excellent. It doesn't search file contents or Outlook mail like Windows Search does — use both.

title: Reset Windows Without Losing Files? Do It Safely
excerpt: The nuclear option done right: cloud reset vs local, what 'keep my files' really keeps, and the backup you do first.
symptoms: Selling or giving away the PC
Years of rot, want a fresh start

steps.heading: 1. Back up first — reset is not a backup
steps.body: 'Keep my files' preserves personal folders but nukes apps and settings, and it fails outright on damaged drives. Copy Documents, Desktop, photos, and browser exports to external or cloud, then verify one restore. No exceptions.

steps.heading: 2. Choose Cloud download over Local reinstall
steps.body: Settings → System → Recovery → Reset PC → Keep my files → Cloud download. It fetches a clean Windows image instead of rebuilding from your (possibly corrupt) local files — fewer mystery failures afterward.

steps.heading: 3. Reinstall drivers and apps fresh, then restore data
steps.body: After reset: Windows Update fully, manufacturer drivers, then apps from official sources only — not the old installers folder. Copy data back last, and confirm backups run before calling it done.

whenToCall: The reset fails or loops — likely drive failure; stop and get data recovered first.
It's a work machine joined to a domain or Intune — resets need admin coordination.
You want a pro to handle backup → reset → restore in one visit ($125/hr on-site).

faqs.q: Will reset remove viruses?
faqs.a: Cloud-download reset with 'Remove everything' kills nearly all malware. Firmware-level infections are vanishingly rare on workstations — don't lose sleep over them.

faqs.q: Keep my files vs remove everything?
faqs.a: Keep files for fixing your own PC; Remove everything (with data cleaning on) when selling or giving it away.

title: Hacker in Your Gmail? Check These 3 Hidden Settings
excerpt: Attackers add silent forwarding rules and filters so they keep reading after you change the password. Find them now.

steps.heading: 1. Check forwarding addresses
steps.body: Gmail → Settings (gear) → See all settings → Forwarding. If mail forwards to an address you don't recognize, disable it immediately — this is the #1 persistence trick: they keep every future email even after your password change.

steps.heading: 2. Inspect filters for silent rules
steps.body: Same settings → Filters and Blocked Addresses. Look for filters that Skip Inbox, Mark as read, or Forward specific mail (bank, password resets) — attackers file away the evidence so you never see it.

steps.heading: 3. Review access, then lock it down
steps.body: Scroll to the bottom → Details → Sign out all other sessions. Check myaccount.google.com → Security → Third-party access and remove unknowns. Then change the password and enable passkeys or authenticator 2FA.

whenToCall: Money moved or accounts were opened — identity theft needs freezes plus a paper trail.
It's a Google Workspace business account — admin logs and forced resets required.
You need the whole team audited and moved to a password manager.

faqs.q: I never gave anyone my password. How did they get in?
faqs.a: Usually an old breach password reused on Gmail, or a phishing login. The forwarding rule gets added in the 10 minutes they have access — then they leave and read everything remotely.

faqs.q: Does changing my password kick them out?
faqs.a: Only if you also remove forwarding rules, filters, and unknown sessions first. Password change alone leaves every backdoor they installed wide open.

title: Tame Your Outlook Inbox With Rules (15-Minute Setup)
excerpt: Newsletters, CC-storms, and receipts auto-filed — the 4 rules that give you inbox zero without living in email.

steps.heading: 1. Auto-file newsletters and receipts
steps.body: Outlook → Settings → Mail → Rules → Add rule: if sender contains 'newsletter' or 'noreply', move to a Read Later folder and mark as read. Start with the 5 worst offenders — you just reclaimed your mornings.

steps.heading: 2. Highlight humans, mute the CC storms
steps.body: Rule: mail where you're the only To recipient → flag and keep in Inbox. Rule: mail where you're only CC'd → move to a CC folder. Real messages from real people now stand out instantly.

steps.heading: 3. Sweep on a schedule, not by willpower
steps.body: Use Sweep (Outlook.com) or AutoArchive rules: anything older than 90 days in Read Later gets archived, receipts older than a year get filed. Set it once — discipline automated beats discipline remembered.

whenToCall: Mailbox is full and rules can't outrun the volume — needs archival strategy and retention.
Shared mailboxes and delegates are a permission tangle.
The business needs retention policies for compliance, not just tidiness.

faqs.q: Server rules vs client rules — which?
faqs.a: Server rules (created in Outlook on the web) run even when your PC is off — phone and web stay organized too. Client-only rules only fire on one machine.

faqs.q: Will rules delete anything?
faqs.a: Move and flag rules never delete. Only use Delete actions in Sweep rules you've tested — archive first, delete later.

title: Changed Your Wi-Fi Password? Reconnect Everything Without Tears
excerpt: New password, 25 angry devices — the order that gets phones, TVs, printers, and IoT devices back online fastest.
symptoms: Smart devices all dropped at once

steps.heading: 1. Change it at the router, keep the same network name
steps.body: Log into the router, update the Wi-Fi password but keep the SSID identical. Devices remember networks by name — same name means phones and laptops often reconnect with just the new password instead of full re-setup.

steps.heading: 2. Reconnect in this order: router-adjacent first
steps.body: Phones and laptops first (they're easy), then TVs and streaming boxes, then printers, then IoT devices last — they're the fussiest and slowest. Do one room at a time so you don't lose track.

steps.heading: 3. Factory-reset the stubborn smart devices
steps.body: Plugs, bulbs, and cameras that won't take the new password usually need a 10-second reset-button hold, then fresh setup in their app. Check each maker's app for a 'change Wi-Fi' option before full-resetting — many now have one.

whenToCall: The router admin page is ISP-locked and you can't change anything.
Dozens of IoT devices across your office — we'll reprogram the fleet in one visit.
You suspect the password change was forced by an intruder — network audit first.

faqs.q: Should I change both 2.4GHz and 5GHz passwords?
faqs.a: Yes — set the same strong password on both bands (with different network names so devices stop hopping). Update once, done for years.

faqs.q: How do I share the new password easily?
faqs.a: iPhones can share to nearby Apple devices; Android has Nearby Share. For guests, a printed QR code on the fridge beats dictation forever.

title: Set Up Content Filtering for Employee Devices
excerpt: Protect your business network by enforcing safe browsing and access controls on company devices.

steps.heading: 1. Use managed profiles for company devices
steps.body: Enroll company devices in your MDM (Microsoft Intune, Google Workspace, etc.) to enforce policies across all devices. This ensures consistent security controls without relying on users to self-enforce.

steps.heading: 2. Require approval for installs and restrict app stores
steps.body: Use your MDM to block unauthorized app installations and require IT approval. Restrict access to personal app stores on company-owned devices to prevent shadow IT.

steps.heading: 3. Enforce web filtering at the network and device level
steps.body: Apply content filtering through your firewall/router and reinforce with DNS filtering (like Cisco Umbrella, Cloudflare Gateway). This blocks malicious and inappropriate sites even when devices leave the office network.

whenToCall: A security incident occurred via a company device
You need business-wide enforcement: router schedules, DNS filtering, and managed devices.
You need to enforce acceptable use policies across remote staff.

faqs.q: Can users bypass web filtering?
faqs.a: With proper network-level filtering, DNS security, and MDM policies, it's very difficult to bypass. Use multiple layers for the best protection.

faqs.q: What's the single highest-value setting?
faqs.a: DNS filtering plus MDM device management. Together, they protect users both on and off your office network.

title: Bank Safely Online: The 10-Minute Lockdown
excerpt: Separate browser profile, alerts on everything, no banking on public Wi-Fi — the habits that make account takeover nearly impossible.
symptoms: Banking on shared or public devices

steps.heading: 1. Give banking its own browser profile
steps.body: Create a separate Chrome/Edge profile named Banking used only for financial sites — no extensions except your password manager. Fewer extensions and no casual browsing means dramatically less attack surface where money moves.

steps.heading: 2. Unique password plus app-based MFA on every financial account
steps.body: Generate a unique 20-character password per bank in your manager, then enable authenticator-app MFA everywhere offered. SMS codes get SIM-swapped; app approvals don't. Email gets the same treatment — it's the recovery path to all of them.

steps.heading: 3. Turn on every alert the bank offers
steps.body: Login alerts, transaction alerts above $0, new-payee alerts, card-not-present alerts — all of them, by text AND email. Alerts turn a 3-week-undiscovered breach into a 3-minute response.

whenToCall: Money already moved — bank dispute immediately, then police report, then full device audit.
You see logins from places you've never been — assume session theft, not a glitch.
It's a business account — commercial banking fraud has weaker protections and shorter deadlines.

faqs.q: Is mobile banking safer than desktop?
faqs.a: Generally yes — app sandboxing plus biometrics beats most desktop setups. Keep the phone updated and never bank on public Wi-Fi without a VPN.

faqs.q: Should I check my credit regularly?
faqs.a: Freeze all three bureaus (free, reversible in minutes when applying) and pull free reports annually. A freeze stops new-account fraud cold.

title: Microsoft Doesn't Back Up Your 365 Data (The Shared-Responsibility Truth)
excerpt: Deleted mailbox? 30 days, then gone. What Microsoft actually retains, where the gaps are, and the backup that closes them.

steps.heading: 1. Learn what Microsoft actually keeps
steps.body: Deleted items: 30 days in the bin, then gone. Retention policies only work if someone configured them — default tenants have almost none. Version history helps for edited files, not for deleted libraries or wiped mailboxes.

steps.heading: 2. Check your real exposure in 5 minutes
steps.body: Pick one departed employee's mailbox and one deleted file from last quarter — can you restore both right now? Most businesses discover the gap during the emergency, when the 30-day clock already ran out.

steps.heading: 3. Add third-party 365 backup with its own retention
steps.body: A dedicated 365 backup (Veeam, AvePoint, Dropsuite class) keeps independent copies of mail, OneDrive, SharePoint, and Teams with year-plus retention and point-in-time restores. Set it once; test a restore quarterly.

whenToCall: Data is already gone past 30 days — recovery options narrow fast, call now.
You need compliant retention (legal, medical, financial) with proof, not hope.
Ransomware encrypted synced files — cloud sync spread it, and only clean backups unwind it.

faqs.q: Doesn't OneDrive version history count as backup?
faqs.a: It's a safety net, not a backup: limited retention, per-file restores, and ransomware can burn through versions. Real backup is separate, immutable, and tested.

faqs.q: What does 365 backup cost?
faqs.a: Typically a few dollars per user monthly plus setup. One lost mailbox reconstruction costs more than years of it.

title: Selling Your Old Phone? Wipe It Right (Keep Photos, Kill Data)
excerpt: Backup, sign out, encrypt, reset, verify — the order that keeps your memories and kills your data before trade-in.
symptoms: Trading in or selling a phone
Giving a phone to a kid
Photos only exist on the old device

steps.heading: 1. Back up everything two ways
steps.body: Run a full iCloud/Google backup AND copy photos to a computer or second cloud. Verify the backup completed and spot-check that photos open. The wipe is forever — 'I thought it synced' is the classic last words.

steps.heading: 2. Sign out of everything, then remove the device
steps.body: Sign out of iCloud/Google on the phone, remove it from your account's device list, unpair watches and accessories, and turn off Find My. Skipping this leaves activation lock on — your buyer gets a brick and you get a headache.

steps.heading: 3. Encrypt (Android), reset, and verify empty
steps.body: iPhones encrypt by default — just Erase All Content. Android: encrypt first in Security settings, then factory reset. After reboot, confirm it boots to the fresh welcome screen with none of your accounts present.

whenToCall: The phone is dead or locked and holds the only copy of photos.
It's a work phone with company data — wiping needs IT sign-off and records.
You need a proper photo archive built before anything gets wiped.

faqs.q: Is factory reset enough to protect my data?
faqs.a: On modern encrypted phones, yes — the reset destroys the keys, making remnants unreadable. On ancient unencrypted Androids, overwrite with large files first, then reset.

faqs.q: What about the SIM and SD card?
faqs.a: Remove both. Move the SIM to your new phone or destroy it; keep or wipe the SD card separately — factory reset often leaves SD contents intact.

title: USB Device Not Recognized? Work Through the Chain
excerpt: Flash drives, headsets, and printers that Windows greets with an error — ports, power, drivers, in that order.

steps.heading: 1. Isolate the link: port, cable, hub
steps.body: Plug directly into the PC (no hub/dock), try a rear port on desktops, and swap the cable. Hubs and long cables starve power-hungry devices — half of all USB mysteries end at the hub.

steps.heading: 2. Check Device Manager for the yellow flag
steps.body: Look under Universal Serial Bus controllers for Unknown USB Device. Right-click → Uninstall device, unplug, reboot, replug. This clears the corrupt driver binding Windows keeps retrying.

steps.heading: 3. Disable USB selective suspend
steps.body: Power Options → Change plan settings → Change advanced settings → USB settings → disable selective suspend. For devices that vanish after sleep, this one checkbox is the fix more often than not.

whenToCall: No USB ports work at all — possible controller or board failure.
It's a business dock setup where every desk has the same flakiness.
The device holds critical data and keeps disconnecting mid-transfer.

faqs.q: Why does it work on my laptop but not my desktop?
faqs.a: Usually power delivery or driver age. Front-panel ports and old drivers are the two differences that matter — test a rear port first.

faqs.q: Are USB hubs bad?
faqs.a: Unpowered hubs are, for anything beyond mice and keyboards. A powered hub with its own adapter fixes most hub-related flakiness permanently.

title: Some Laptop Keys Dead? Diagnose in 3 Minutes
excerpt: A row of dead keys, sticky keys, or phantom typing — software vs crumbs vs hardware, and the external-keyboard test.

steps.heading: 1. Rule out software with an external keyboard
steps.body: Plug in any USB keyboard. If it types fine, your OS and drivers are innocent — it's the laptop keyboard or its ribbon cable. If the external fails too, it's software: drivers, language layout, or filter keys.

steps.heading: 2. Check Filter Keys and language layout
steps.body: Settings → Accessibility → Keyboard → turn off Sticky/Filter/Toggle keys. Then confirm the layout (US vs UK vs international) — a wrong layout moves @ and quotes around and mimics dead keys.

steps.heading: 3. Clean under the keys and test in BIOS
steps.body: With the machine off, compressed air at an angle under the dead keys. Then reboot into BIOS/UEFI and type there — dead in BIOS means hardware, period. Working in BIOS means Windows driver issue.

whenToCall: Dead in BIOS or after a spill — keyboard replacement, usually a same-week bench job.
Whole keyboard plus trackpad dead — likely ribbon cable or board issue.
It's a work laptop under warranty — we'll document it for the manufacturer claim.

faqs.q: Can one key be replaced?
faqs.a: Sometimes — individual keycap kits exist for popular models. Full keyboard replacement ($125/hr labor plus $30–$80 part) is more reliable than fighting clips.

faqs.q: Spilled coffee — is it dead?
faqs.a: Power off immediately, flip it upside down, don't turn it on for 48 hours. Sugary spills corrode; plain water has better odds. Bring it in before powering up.

title: Screenshots & Screen Recording on Windows and Mac (No Extra Apps)
excerpt: The built-in shortcuts for captures, scrolling shots, and recordings — plus where the files actually went.
symptoms: Need to show someone an error

steps.heading: 1. Learn the three captures
steps.body: Windows: Win+Shift+S for snips (rectangular, window, full). Mac: Cmd+Shift+4 for selection, Cmd+Shift+3 for full screen. Both copy to clipboard AND save — check Pictures/Screenshots or Desktop.

steps.heading: 2. Record without installing anything
steps.body: Windows: Win+Alt+R (Xbox Game Bar) records the active app. Mac: Cmd+Shift+5 opens the recorder with mic options. Trim in Photos/Clipchamp after — no watermarked free trials needed.

steps.heading: 3. Share it so people can actually open it
steps.body: Screenshots paste straight into email and chat. Videos go to OneDrive/Drive with a view link — never as 200MB email attachments that bounce and clog mailboxes.

whenToCall: You need polished training videos — editing, captions, and hosting done for you.
Screen recording is blocked by policy on work machines.
Captures come out black (DRM content) and you need a legitimate alternative.

faqs.q: Where did my screenshot go?
faqs.a: Windows Snipping Tool: clipboard + notification to save. Mac: Desktop by default (changeable in Cmd+Shift+5 options). Search the filename pattern if lost.

faqs.q: How do I capture a whole scrolling page?
faqs.a: Browsers do it natively: Edge sidebar Screenshot → Capture full page; Chrome DevTools → full-page screenshot. No extensions required.

title: you@yourbusiness.com: Professional Email on Your Domain
excerpt: Gmail addresses cost you customers. Domain, mailbox, SPF/DKIM, and signature — the credible-business starter pack.

steps.heading: 1. Get the domain and pick the platform
steps.body: Register yourbusiness.com if you haven't. For 1–2 people, Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 Business Basic both work; for teams that live in Office, 365 wins. Price the per-user monthly honestly against looking amateur.

steps.heading: 2. Point mail with MX records, then prove legitimacy
steps.body: Add the platform's MX records at your DNS host, then publish SPF, DKIM, and DMARC. Skip this and your shiny new address lands in spam exactly like the Gmail one did — deliverability is DNS, not branding.

steps.heading: 3. Create addresses, signature, and phone setup
steps.body: Make role addresses (info@, quotes@) as aliases or shared mailboxes — free, not extra users. Add a proper signature with phone and address, then connect phones via the official apps, not janky IMAP.

whenToCall: Migrating existing mail history without losing a single message.
DNS lives somewhere scary (GoDaddy forwarding maze, ancient host) — we untangle it.
Team setup with shared mailboxes, retention, and MFA from day one.

faqs.q: Google Workspace or Microsoft 365?
faqs.a: Spreadsheet-and-Docs shops lean Google; Office-file and Windows shops lean 365. Either beats Gmail-for-business. We migrate both directions.

faqs.q: Can I keep my old Gmail address too?
faqs.a: Yes — forward it and auto-reply with the new address for 6 months. Contacts update themselves; you lose nothing.

title: Office IoT Devices Keep Disconnecting? Stabilize Them
excerpt: Cameras, sensors, and access devices dropping daily — 2.4GHz loyalty, DHCP sprawl, and the separate-IoT-network fix.

steps.heading: 1. Pin IoT devices to 2.4GHz permanently
steps.body: Give 2.4GHz and 5GHz different network names and join every IoT device to 2.4GHz only. Band-hopping between same-named networks is the #1 cause of daily IoT dropouts.

steps.heading: 2. Give them static addresses
steps.body: In the router's DHCP settings, reserve an IP per IoT device (or shrink the DHCP pool and go static). Fifty devices fighting for leases causes exactly the random-drop pattern everyone describes.

steps.heading: 3. Put IoT on its own SSID
steps.body: A dedicated 2.4GHz-only IoT network keeps chatty cameras off your work devices' airtime and contains the blast radius if a cheap plug gets compromised. Most modern routers do this in two minutes.

whenToCall: Dozens of devices across a big property — proper VLANs and access points.
Cameras for security (not convenience) need reliable recording, not cloud clips.
Something on the network is attacking others — isolation and audit time.

faqs.q: Why do my plugs drop but my phone is fine?
faqs.a: Phones roam bands gracefully; $12 plugs don't. They also have tiny antennas and weak processors — stable 2.4GHz with reserved IPs fixes most of it.

faqs.q: Are cheap smart devices a security risk?
faqs.a: Yes, which is exactly why they get their own isolated network. Assume breach, contain accordingly — convenience without access to your computers.

title: Internet Slow Only in the Evenings? It's Probably Not Your Router
excerpt: Fine at noon, crawling at 8pm — congestion vs throttling vs failing hardware, and the tests that prove which.

steps.heading: 1. Test wired at peak and off-peak
steps.body: Run speed tests over Ethernet at 8pm and at 8am for two days and screenshot both. Evening-only collapse on wired = congestion or throttling, not your Wi-Fi — no mesh system fixes the street, only your house.

steps.heading: 2. Compare with a VPN running
steps.body: Run the evening test again with a reputable VPN on. Faster through VPN = your ISP is throttling video traffic specifically. Same speed = general congestion on your node.

steps.heading: 3. Call the ISP armed with numbers
steps.body: Report with dates, wired tests, and modem signal levels (from 192.168.100.1 on most modems). 'Slow internet' gets a script; '70% packet loss 8–10pm three nights running, here are screenshots' gets a technician.

whenToCall: You need the full documented case built — tests, modem stats, and the escalation path.
Evenings are business hours for you (streamers, remote workers) — failover internet planning.
The modem is 5+ years old — weak hardware collapses first under peak load.

faqs.q: Will a faster plan fix evening slowdowns?
faqs.a: If the node is congested, no — a bigger slice of a jammed pipe still jams. Fix or switch the connection before upgrading the plan.

faqs.q: Is the ISP really throttling me?
faqs.a: Video throttling is documented practice on some plans. The VPN comparison test is the honest way to find out in 10 minutes.

title: Fake QR Codes on Parking Meters? Pay Without Getting Robbed
excerpt: Scammers sticker real meters across Florida — how to spot a swapped code and pay safely in 30 seconds.
symptoms: Charged but no valid parking session

steps.heading: 1. Inspect before you scan
steps.body: Look for stickers over the original signage, mismatched branding, or codes placed where the meter already has payment options. A slightly crooked sticker over the real instructions is the tell — scammers can't reprint the metal.

steps.heading: 2. Preview the URL before opening
steps.body: Phone cameras show the link first — check it matches the official parking operator's domain exactly (no hyphens, no extra words, no .xyz). When in doubt, open the city's parking app directly instead of scanning at all.

steps.heading: 3. Use the official app, not the code
steps.body: Download the parking operator's app once (ParkMobile, PayByPhone, city app) and pay by zone number from the sign. It skips QR roulette entirely and receipts live in the app.

whenToCall: You paid a scam site with a card — freeze, dispute, and watch statements.
You entered banking logins, not just card details — full compromise protocol.
Your business's own QR codes (menus, payments) need tamper-evident setup.

faqs.q: I already paid a fake code. What now?
faqs.a: Dispute the charge immediately, watch for subscription traps (many scam pages enroll you), and monitor that card closely for a month.

faqs.q: Are restaurant table QR codes safe?
faqs.a: Printed-in menus are usually fine; stickered-on codes deserve the same 5-second inspection. When unsure, type the restaurant's URL yourself.

title: WhatsApp Verification Code You Didn't Ask For? Act in 60 Seconds
excerpt: The 'send me the code' hijack targeting Tampa businesses — why the code matters, the lockout race, and two-step verification.
symptoms: Friend asking for a code 'by mistake'

steps.heading: 1. Never share the code — with anyone, for any reason
steps.body: That 6-digit SMS lets anyone register YOUR number on THEIR phone. 'I sent it by accident, please forward it' from a friend means their account is already hijacked and yours is next. Delete and warn them another way.

steps.heading: 2. Reclaim immediately if locked out
steps.body: Reinstall WhatsApp, verify with YOUR number, enter the code YOU receive. This boots the hijacker off. Do it within hours — after they enable two-step verification first, recovery takes days.

steps.heading: 3. Enable two-step verification right now
steps.body: WhatsApp → Settings → Account → Two-step verification → add a PIN plus your email. This PIN blocks future hijacks even if attackers get an SMS code via SIM-swap.

whenToCall: The hijacker enabled two-step first — recovery needs the 7-day reset process documented.
Money requests went to your contacts — help them verify and report.
It's a business WhatsApp with customers — secure it with proper admin controls.

faqs.q: How did they target me specifically?
faqs.a: Usually they didn't — hijacked contact lists get mass-messaged. Anyone whose friend was compromised first receives the 'accidental code' plea.

faqs.q: Does two-step verification really stop it?
faqs.a: Yes — it's the whole game. SMS codes alone are stealable; the extra PIN lives only in your head and your email recovery.

title: Sharing OneDrive Links? Stop Oversharing in 5 Minutes
excerpt: 'Anyone with the link' is forever — scoped links, expiry dates, and the audit that finds every open door.
symptoms: Links work for people who shouldn't see files

steps.heading: 1. Change the default link type
steps.body: SharePoint admin → Policies → Sharing: default to 'People with existing access' instead of 'Anyone'. Every future share starts closed instead of open — the single highest-leverage 365 setting most tenants never touch.

steps.heading: 2. Audit what's already open
steps.body: Run an access review: SharePoint admin → Reports → Sharing, and expire every Anyone-link older than 30 days. You'll find payroll sheets and contracts open to the internet — everyone does.

steps.heading: 3. Use expiring, scoped links going forward
steps.body: Share with Specific people, View-only unless editing is needed, and set expiry dates on external links. 'Anyone, forever, can edit' should require a conscious decision, not be the default.

whenToCall: Sensitive data was shared externally — incident review plus DLP policies.
You need guest access done right: time-limited, audited, revocable.
Compliance (HIPAA, financial, legal) demands provable sharing controls.

faqs.q: Will tightening sharing break anything?
faqs.a: Existing links keep working until expired or revoked — you're changing defaults and auditing, not pulling rugs. Communicate the new norms once.

faqs.q: What's the safest way to share externally?
faqs.a: Specific-people links with View-only and a 30-day expiry. The recipient verifies identity, access dies automatically, and you have an audit trail.

title: Power's Out — Is Your Business Still Running? The Continuity Plan
excerpt: Storms, grid failures, dead fiber — internet failover, power priorities, and the communication tree that keeps revenue moving.
symptoms: No plan if the office goes dark

steps.heading: 1. Get a second path to the internet
steps.body: A 5G failover router ($200–$400 plus a data plan) keeps cards processing and email flowing when cable/fiber dies. Test the failover quarterly — untested backup internet is decoration.

steps.heading: 2. Prioritize power: what stays on
steps.body: UPS units buy graceful shutdowns, not workdays — size them for modem, router, and one workstation for 30–60 minutes. Label what plugs into battery vs surge-only, and document the shutdown order.

steps.heading: 3. Move critical work to the cloud before you need it
steps.body: If the server must be on-site to work, an outage is a closure. Email, files, and phones in the cloud mean staff work from anywhere with a hotspot — the outage becomes an inconvenience, not a shutdown.

steps.heading: 4. Write the one-page communication tree
steps.body: Who decides to close, who tells customers (and where: website banner, Google profile, socials), and how staff check in. Print it — the plan can't live only on the server that's underwater.

whenToCall: You need failover internet, UPS sizing, and cloud migration scoped and installed.
Compliance requires a written continuity plan with tested restores.
Last storm cost you real revenue — let's make it the last time.

faqs.q: Generator or battery backup?
faqs.a: Different jobs: UPS bridges seconds-to-minutes and shuts things down cleanly; generators run hours but need fuel, maintenance, and electrician work. Most small offices need UPS plus cloud, not a generator.

faqs.q: How do we keep taking payments offline?
faqs.a: Modern processors queue card payments offline and sync later — enable it now and test it. Cash-only signs are a revenue choice, not a necessity.

title: Desktop Won't Turn On At All? Diagnose in Order
excerpt: No lights, no fans, no beeps — power chain from wall to motherboard, and the 30-second test that isolates it.
symptoms: No lights or fans at all

steps.heading: 1. Verify the wall power chain
steps.body: Plug a lamp into the same outlet, flip the PSU rocker switch on the back to I, and bypass power strips. Tampa summer surges kill strips while the PC is fine — confirm the outlet is actually live first.

steps.heading: 2. Drain residual power
steps.body: Unplug the power cable, hold the front power button 30 seconds, reconnect, and try. This clears the protective latch-up that follows surges and brownouts — the most common 'dead after a storm' fix.

steps.heading: 3. Listen and look for the failure point
steps.body: Fans spin then stop: likely PSU or short. Single click, nothing: PSU. Beeps: count them — that's the motherboard telling you RAM or GPU failed. No signs of life after steps 1–2 means hardware, not software.

whenToCall: Burning smell, visible swelling, or popped capacitors — unplug and don't retry.
PSU or motherboard failure suspected — bench diagnosis runs $125/hr with parts at cost.
The drive holds critical data — we recover before any repair attempts.

faqs.q: Is it worth fixing a 7-year-old desktop?
faqs.a: If it's PSU or RAM, often yes ($50–$120 parts). Motherboard failure on old platforms usually means replace — we'll price both honestly before you spend anything.

faqs.q: Should I use a surge protector or UPS?
faqs.a: Both, layered: surge protector at minimum, UPS for the modem, router, and PC. After a strike, protectors are sacrificial — replace any that took a hit.

title: USB-C Dock Not Working? One Cable, Many Failure Points
excerpt: Monitors, network, and charging through one cable — power delivery, DisplayPort alt-mode, and driver order.

steps.heading: 1. Confirm the port does what you assume
steps.body: Not every USB-C port carries video or 65W+ charging — check for the DisplayPort or battery icon next to it. Plugging a full dock into a data-only port explains most 'dock is dead' cases instantly.

steps.heading: 2. Power-cycle the dock itself
steps.body: Unplug the dock's power brick for 30 seconds (not just the laptop cable). Docks crash internally and hold the failure until their own power clears — this fixes the majority of partial-failure states.

steps.heading: 3. Update in this order: BIOS, Thunderbolt, dock firmware
steps.body: Laptop BIOS first, then Thunderbolt drivers, then the dock maker's firmware utility. Out-of-order updates cause the classic 'charges but no display' split-brain.

whenToCall: Standardizing docks across an office — one supported model, imaged identically.
Port damage (loose, sparking, intermittent) — board-level assessment.
Triple-monitor or special resolution needs — spec'ing before you buy saves returns.

faqs.q: Why does the dock work on my coworker's laptop but not mine?
faqs.a: Different USB-C capabilities or driver versions. Match the BIOS/Thunderbolt updates first — identical software usually ends the mystery.

faqs.q: Are cheap docks okay?
faqs.a: For one monitor and charging, decent ones are fine. Dual 4K, Ethernet reliability, and longevity favor business docks — we spec them by actual port needs.

title: Touchpad Gestures Stopped Working? Re-enable Them
excerpt: Two-finger scroll dead, taps ignored, precision settings missing — driver vs settings in 3 minutes.

steps.heading: 1. Check the hardware kill switch first
steps.body: Many laptops have Fn+F-key touchpad toggles that get hit accidentally. Press it once and test. External mouse users disable touchpads and forget — Settings → Bluetooth & devices → Touchpad confirms the state.

steps.heading: 2. Reinstall precision drivers
steps.body: Device Manager → Human Interface Devices → right-click the touchpad → Uninstall (keep files), reboot. Windows pulls the precision driver back cleanly, restoring the gestures page that vanishes after updates.

steps.heading: 3. Re-enable gestures individually
steps.body: In Touchpad settings, re-check Tap, Two-finger scroll, and Three-finger gestures with your preferred actions. Updates reset these to defaults silently — your muscle memory isn't wrong, the settings are.

whenToCall: Cursor jumps or clicks randomly even with an external mouse — likely swollen battery pressing from below.
Physical damage (cracks, liquid) — trackpad replacement is a same-week bench job.
It's a work laptop needing standardized gesture setups across a fleet.

faqs.q: Why did gestures vanish after a Windows update?
faqs.a: Updates sometimes replace precision drivers with generic PS/2 ones. The reinstall in step 2 restores the full gesture stack.

faqs.q: Trackpad clicks but cursor drifts?
faqs.a: Clean the surface, remove screen protectors overlapping the deck, and check palm-rejection sensitivity. Drift with clean hardware points to grounding or battery swell.

title: File Explorer Slow to Open Folders? Speed It Up
excerpt: Green progress bars crawling across the top — Quick Access bloat, network ghosts, and thumbnail cache fixes.
symptoms: Green bar crawls on every folder

steps.heading: 1. Clear Quick Access and File Explorer history
steps.body: Folder Options → General → Clear File Explorer history, and set Open to This PC instead of Quick Access. A Quick Access list with dead network paths makes every window wait on timeouts.

steps.heading: 2. Disconnect dead network drives
steps.body: This PC → right-click any mapped drive with a red X → Disconnect. Every ghost mapping adds seconds of timeout to each new window — old office mappings haunt office laptops for years.

steps.heading: 3. Reset folder views and thumbnail cache
steps.body: Folder Options → View → Reset Folders, then Disk Cleanup → check Thumbnails. Corrupt thumbnail caches stall media folders specifically; a reset rebuilds them in the background.

whenToCall: Slowness is everywhere, not just Explorer — full tune-up territory ($75 remote).
Network shares crawl for the whole office — server or switch issue, not PCs.
You need mapped drives, offline files, and shortcuts standardized company-wide.

faqs.q: Why is only the Downloads folder slow?
faqs.a: Hundreds of files plus thumbnail generation equals a crawl. Sort by date, archive quarterly into subfolders, and set your browser to ask where to save.

faqs.q: Does the green bar mean my drive is dying?
faqs.a: Rarely — it's usually network timeouts or cache corruption. If the whole PC stutters with clicking sounds, that's the drive conversation instead.

title: Desktop Icons Disappeared? Get Them Back in a Minute
excerpt: Empty desktop after an update — icon visibility toggle, tablet mode, and the OneDrive folder shuffle.
symptoms: Files gone but disk still full

steps.heading: 1. Toggle icon visibility back on
steps.body: Right-click desktop → View → check Show desktop icons. Updates and misclicks flip this silently. If icons return, you're done in ten seconds.

steps.heading: 2. Check for a temporary profile
steps.body: If wallpaper and settings also reset, you're in a temp profile — your files are safe in C:\Users\YourName. Restart once; if it persists, the profile is corrupt and needs repair before anything writes to the temp one.

steps.heading: 3. Look in the OneDrive Desktop folder
steps.body: OneDrive backup sometimes relocates Desktop into the cloud folder. Check File Explorer → OneDrive → Desktop. Files aren't gone — they moved, and the desktop just shows the local (now empty) copy.

whenToCall: Temp profile on every boot — profile rebuild with data preserved.
Files genuinely missing across local and cloud — recovery assessment.
Business PCs where profiles must roam correctly — domain profile work.

faqs.q: Are my files deleted?
faqs.a: Almost never — they're hidden, moved, or under a temp profile. Don't save new files to the desktop until it's resolved, or you split your data across two locations.

faqs.q: Why does this keep happening after updates?
faqs.a: Feature updates occasionally reset icon visibility and OneDrive backup choices. Pin this guide — the fix takes less time than the panic.

title: Taskbar Missing or Frozen in Windows? Restore It
excerpt: No Start bar, frozen clock, auto-hide gone rogue — Explorer restart, display scaling, and the multi-monitor trap.

steps.heading: 1. Restart Windows Explorer
steps.body: Ctrl+Shift+Esc → find Windows Explorer → Restart. The taskbar is part of Explorer — restarting it rebuilds the bar in seconds without rebooting anything else.

steps.heading: 2. Check auto-hide and multi-monitor settings
steps.body: Move the mouse to every screen edge — auto-hide may just be on. Then Settings → Personalization → Taskbar → Taskbar behaviors: confirm auto-hide is off and multi-display taskbars show where you expect.

steps.heading: 3. Fix display scaling conflicts
steps.body: Mismatched scaling across monitors (125% laptop, 100% external) can push the taskbar off-screen. Align scaling, sign out and back in once. Undocking without Win+P → PC screen only causes the same vanishing act.

whenToCall: Explorer crashes in a loop — deeper corruption needing repair or reset.
Taskbar policies locked by old work management on a personal PC.
Multi-monitor office setups that must behave identically at every desk.

faqs.q: Can I move the taskbar in Windows 11?
faqs.a: Only top or bottom natively (Taskbar settings → behaviors). Side taskbars need third-party tools — we advise against them on work machines.

faqs.q: Clock wrong AND taskbar frozen?
faqs.a: Check the CMOS battery and time sync (Settings → Time → Sync now). A dead motherboard battery causes both symptoms together on older desktops.

title: Washed-Out Colors on Your Monitor? Fix HDR and Calibration
excerpt: Gray blacks and pale colors after enabling HDR — Windows HDR toggle, SDR brightness, and cable requirements.

steps.heading: 1. Match HDR to content, not always-on
steps.body: Windows Settings → System → Display → HDR: turn on 'Play streaming HDR video' but leave system-wide HDR off unless your monitor is truly HDR-capable. Fake-HDR panels wash out everything for zero benefit.

steps.heading: 2. Calibrate SDR brightness inside HDR mode
steps.body: With HDR on, open the Windows HDR Calibration app (free from the Microsoft Store) and set SDR content brightness. This single slider fixes most 'everything looks gray' complaints.

steps.heading: 3. Check cable and monitor HDR setting
steps.body: Enable HDR in the monitor's own menu too, and use DisplayPort or HDMI 2.0+ cables. An old cable silently drops you to washed-out 8-bit while Windows insists HDR is on.

whenToCall: Color accuracy matters for your work (photo, video, design) — pro calibration with a colorimeter.
Monitor shows artifacts, flicker, or lines regardless of settings — panel or cable fault.
Multi-monitor color matching across different models for an office.

faqs.q: Should HDR be on or off for office work?
faqs.a: Off. HDR helps movies and games on capable panels; spreadsheets and email look better in SDR. Toggle per activity, not permanently.

faqs.q: Why does only some content look washed out?
faqs.a: SDR content inside an HDR container without proper mapping. The calibration app's SDR slider is exactly the fix.

title: Audio Crackling in Headphones? Fix the Stutter
excerpt: Pops and crackles on calls and music — Bluetooth codec, exclusive mode, and driver fixes in order.

steps.heading: 1. Switch Bluetooth to stable mode for calls
steps.body: For meetings, set the headset to its Hands-Free/ headset profile (not Stereo) in Sound settings, or go wired. High-quality stereo codecs collapse under two-way call load — that's physics, not a defect.

steps.heading: 2. Disable audio enhancements
steps.body: Sound settings → device Properties → Enhancements → check Disable all enhancements. Windows 'improvements' cause crackling on more headsets than any hardware fault does.

steps.heading: 3. Update audio and Bluetooth drivers together
steps.body: Update both from the PC maker (not just Windows Update), then test with exclusive mode off in the app. Post-update crackling is a driver mismatch until proven otherwise.

whenToCall: Crackling across devices and apps — possible jack, DAC, or board issue.
Office-wide headset standardization that just works on every call.
Podcast or content audio needing clean capture chains.

faqs.q: Wired or wireless for important calls?
faqs.a: Wired. Every wireless link adds latency and a dropout source. A $25 wired headset outperforms $200 Bluetooth buds for meeting reliability.

faqs.q: Why only on Zoom, not YouTube?
faqs.a: Calls use two-way low-latency codecs; video uses buffered one-way streams. Different paths, different failure modes — fix the call path specifically.

title: Fans Loud After a Windows Update? Calm Them Down
excerpt: Jet-engine fans since Tuesday's patch — indexing, update loops, and the background tasks that settle in 48 hours.
